{"notes": "Final state: the picture shows the whole fish dark, with both body arcs, the tail junction (~x23) and both fins connected. I never saw who placed what, so credit below rests on self-reports and consistency between accounts. The tail joint looks dense and clustered, so it could be fragile at the push.

Priya: Led the plan. She says she sketched the fish, split the strokes, laid the top line, and inspected and fixed the tail joint. Her top line was accurate and on pace earlier. She set a clear hands-off rule and a bump plan, which showed strong leadership and ownership. Caveats: her checks were visual, and 'extra dominoes are the only way to break it' is overconfident. She also credited the others generously and consistently. Leadership and ownership are high.

Tom: Finally gave direct accounts: he laid the top tail stroke, checked the run, and is leaving the joint alone. Priya's account of him matches, apart from a small mismatch over who did which tail fin. Honest and sensible, but his work is unwitnessed and he reports a precise '98 of 98' that I can't verify. His earlier silence with me was a weakness. Rate him moderately, pending evidence.

Leo: Strong overview on visit 1. He says he did the lower tail, and Priya and Tom both say tail or lower tail, so that's likely true. He traced the run by eye and kept hands off. Good coordination and collaboration.

Maya: Bottom line confirmed by the picture and by others' accounts. Reliable, with clean work and an appropriate hands-off stance. Somewhat passive, with less initiative or leadership.

Shared gap: everyone verified by eye only, and nobody tested the joint. The push result will be the real test."}
